what: EXACTLY-2-SPLIT bounded decider for s=111's tree question
engine: hec.two_split_enumerator (enumerate 2-split leaf-colored trees; exact weight fit; chordality+coarse-grain certificate)

enum_completeness.out_of_scope: known tree has a degree>1 boundary vertex; colored_trees enumerates leaf-boundary trees only — this tree is outside the enumeration scope (a real bound on the search), so completeness is N/A for it

B.note: rays 10/17 known trees are 3-split; a 2-split negative for them is EXPECTED (not a bug). Validated via lift-certify + fit-recovery on the known trees (blind 3-split enumeration is the same 9-leaf wall as s=111).

info.qualifier: BOUNDED: no realization of s=111 found via EXACTLY 2 split(s), each into <= 2 sub-parties, over 4186 distinct (pynauty-canonical) leaf-colored tree structures. ALL split pairs were covered up to n_bulk=2 (breadth-first); n_bulk=3 was only PARTIALLY covered — search TRUNCATED by the time budget. This negative is bounded by (i) the exactly-2-split/m/bulk enumeration AND the leaf-boundary restriction of colored_trees (boundary vertices must be tree leaves — multi-split trees with a degree>1 boundary vertex are out of scope), (ii) the caps just noted, and (iii) the HEURISTIC weight fit (a fit miss is not a proof the structure cannot realize v). NOT a proof that no tree realization exists; NOT a statement about realizability (the ray is holographic).

s111.interpretation: BOUNDED NEGATIVE: no EXACTLY-2-SPLIT (each into 2) tree realizes s=111 across 4186 distinct (pynauty-canonical) leaf-colored tree structures. ALL 21 split-pairs were FULLY covered through n_bulk=2 (3024 structures); deeper n_bulk only partially. The negative is bounded by (i) the exactly-2-split / m=2 enumeration AND colored_trees' leaf-boundary restriction, (ii) n_bulk coverage + the time budget, (iii) the heuristic weight fit — at settings (descents=10,cut_rounds=8,attempts=2) that DEMONSTRABLY recover the known rays-10/17 3-split trees, so this is a fit that finds realizable structures, not a toothless one. NOT a proof no tree exists; s=111 is holographic; decides only the 2-split question. WHERE 2 SPLITS EXPLODE: the leaf-colored tree count grows steeply with bulk size (1 star at n_bulk=1; 143/pair at n_bulk=2; >1000/pair at n_bulk=3 — one pair's n_bulk=3 alone did not finish in ~11 min), so full n_bulk>=3 across 21 pairs is hours-to-days. With the per-fit cost tamed (the cut_rounds cap cut a pathological 30s fit to 0.25s), the wall is now the CANDIDATE COUNT (tree growth in n_bulk), not the per-candidate fit.

fit_power_check.note: the sweep fit recovers known realizable trees -> the s=111 negative is credible
